title: How often do you step out of the house?
description: A long project counts how many times a person steps out of the house each day. Ten sample days are shown on a dot plot, and the mean, median and range are found to describe the data.
teaching_notes: One idea: a day with zero counts is a real value and stays in the data. Watch for children who leave out the zero days when they find the mean.

video_script.why: The child can read a dot plot and find a mean and a median, and now collects a long run of their own data.
video_script.substitution: Ten sample days stand in for the month of counts the book asks for.
video_script.anchor: Sample data for ten days: 3, 2, 4, 1, 0, 5, 3, 2, 6, 4 times stepping out of the house
video_script.payoff_line: For the sample, the mean and median are three and the range is six.

final_answer.value: For the sample: mean 3, median 3, range 6; record your own month and use the same steps
final_answer.spoken: for the sample, the mean and median are three and the range is six

maths_rules: dot plot on a line from 0 to 6: one dot each at 0, 1, 5 and 6, and two dots each at 2, 3 and 4
range 6 - 0 = 6; a day at home counts as 0, a real value
check: pairs from the two ends 0 + 6, 1 + 5, 2 + 4, 2 + 4, 3 + 3 each make 6; five pairs make 30
video_script.design: One number line from zero to six with a stack of dots on each count, then the mean and median marked on it.
open_questions: The book asks for a month of the viewer's own counts, so the ten days are sample data from the worklist, labelled sample on screen.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a project from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>You track how many times you step out of your house in a day.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>You do this for a month, and some days you may not step out at all.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How can we describe all these counts together?

beats.on_screen: the door and the calendar stay on the board

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a dot plot with one dot for each day; the middle of the sorted list labelled median; the gap from least to greatest labelled range

marks.m1: dots stand on a number line, one for each day
marks.m2: the middle of the sorted counts is labelled median
marks.m3: the gap from the least to the greatest is drawn and labelled range
marks.m4: the hint line the same way as the book's example glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A dot plot puts one dot on a number line for each day.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The middle of the sorted list is called the median.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The gap between the greatest and the least is called the range.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Given (sample), steps out on ten days: 3, 2, 4, 1, 0, 5, 3, 2, 6, 4

marks.m1: the word sample and the first five counts are written
marks.m2: the last five counts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the sample counts for ten days. The first five days are three, two, four, one and zero.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The next five days are five, three, two, six and four.

beats.on_screen: To find: a dot plot; the mean, median and range of the counts

marks.m1: the tasks are written under the counts

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to make a dot plot, and describe the typical count and how far the counts spread.

beats.on_screen: number line from 0 to 6; dots: 0 has 1, 1 has 1, 2 has 2, 3 has 2, 4 has 2, 5 has 1, 6 has 1

marks.m1: the number line from 0 to 6 is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, draw the dot plot. Use a number line from zero to six, and put one dot for each day.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Zero has one dot, one has one dot, and two has two dots.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three has two dots, four has two dots, and five and six have one dot each.

marks.m1: the ten counts are added and 30 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, find the mean. The ten counts add up to thirty, and the zero day adds nothing.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Divide thirty by ten. The mean is three times a day.

marks.m1: the counts are sorted from least to greatest
marks.m2: the fifth and sixth counts glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, sort the counts from least to greatest, and find the middle.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>With ten values, the median is halfway between the fifth and sixth values. Both of them are three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Half of six is three, so the median is three.

beats.on_screen: range = 6 - 0 = 6; the zero day is a real value and stays in the data

marks.m1: the greatest count 6 and the least count 0 glow
marks.m3: the zero day is outlined as a real value

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, find the range. The greatest count is six and the least is zero.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Six take away zero is six, so the counts spread over six steps.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A day at home is a real value, so the zero stays in the data.

beats.on_screen: check: pair the ends of the sorted list: 0 + 6, 1 + 5, 2 + 4, 2 + 4, 3 + 3, each pair makes 6; 5 pairs make 30

marks.m1: the ends of the sorted list are joined in pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, check the total by pairing the ends of the sorted list.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Zero and six, one and five, and two and four each make six. Another two and four, and three and three, also make six.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Five pairs of six make thirty, which matches the total.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>For the sample, the mean and median are three and the range is six.
